short: Foundational figure of modern nursing whose statistical work transformed public healthcare.
full:
Florence Nightingale defied the expectations of her wealthy family to pursue a career in nursing, travelling to the Crimea in 1854 to manage the care of wounded British soldiers. Appalled by the unsanitary conditions and staggering mortality rates at the Scutari hospital, she implemented rigorous hygiene standards and administrative reforms that drastically reduced deaths from infection.

Returning to Britain as a national heroine, Nightingale used her fame and her pioneering mastery of data visualisation — notably her 'polar area diagram' — to force systematic reform of military and civil healthcare. She established the first secular nursing school at St Thomas' Hospital in London in 1860, elevating nursing into a respected, professionalised medical discipline.
